1.1: This the heavy word the prophet Habakkuk saw comin'.
1.2: Lord, how long I gotta cry out before You hear me? I'm yellin' "Violence!" out here and You ain't savin' nobody.
1.3: Why You keep showin' me all this wickedness? Why You got me watchin' all this mess—robbery, drama, folks wildin' out everywhere?
1.4: The law got no power now, and justice? Man, it don't even show up. Wicked folks got the good folks surrounded, so wrong judgments keep comin' down.
1.5: Look around, all y'all—watch close. I'm 'bout to do somethin' so wild, y'all wouldn't believe it even if somebody told you.
1.6: I'm raisin' up the Chaldeans—yeah, them ruthless, quick-tempered folks. They movin' through lands that don't belong to 'em, takin' over like it's theirs.
1.7: They scary and dangerous—don't answer to nobody. They make they own rules and carry themselves like they gods.
1.8: Their horses faster than leopards, meaner than wolves at night. Them riders pullin' up from way out, movin' like eagles ready to eat.
1.9: They comin' straight for violence— they eyes sharp like that east wind, scoopin' folks up like sand in a bag.
1.10: They laugh at kings, don't respect no prince. Every fortress look like child's play to them—they just stack dirt and take it.
1.11: Then they get cocky, switch up, and go too far. They wrong for it, but still give credit to they fake gods like that's who made it happen.
1.12: Ain't You the everlasting God, Lord? My holy one? We ain't supposed to die like this. Lord, You the one who picked them for judgment. You our Rock. You supposed to check them.
1.13: Your eyes too pure to look at evil, so how You lettin' treacherous folks get away with this? Why You sittin' quiet while the wicked eat up folks more righteous than them?
1.14: You got people lookin' like fish in the sea, like little bugs with nobody to guide 'em.
1.15: These enemies scoopin' everybody up with they nets, pullin' in whole crowds like it's nothin'. And they celebratin'—they hype about it.
1.16: They treat they nets like gods now, burnin' incense and throwin' offerings, 'cause that net got 'em fed real good, got 'em livin' large.
1.17: So what now? They just gon' keep emptyin' that net, keep killin' off nations without even feelin' bad?

2.1: I'ma stay posted at my spot, Watchin' and waitin', up on the lookout tower, Tryna see what the Lord gon' say to me, And how I'm supposed to respond when He checks me.
2.2: Then the Lord hit me with the word: "Write down this vision real clear. Put it on tablets so anybody readin' it can take off runnin' with it.
2.3: This vision got an appointment—it ain't late, it's just not time yet. But when it hits, it's gon' speak loud and won't lie. It might feel like it's takin' forever, but hold tight— It's comin' for sure, no doubt about it."
2.4: "Look at the one who's puffed up— his soul all twisted inside. But the one who's righteous? They gon' live by faith, not by flex."
2.5: That man wildin' with wine, Full of pride, always runnin' the streets. He greedy like the grave—never satisfied. Snatchin' up nations, stackin' folks like trophies.
2.6: But don't think folks ain't gon' talk about him— They gon' roast him with parables and punchlines: 'Woe to the one who stacks what ain't his— How long you think you gon' get away with that? You out here drownin' in debt.'
2.7: Ain't your lenders gon' wake up and say "Run it back"? Ain't your enemies gon' flip the script and rob you this time?
2.8: You tore up many nations—now the leftovers gon' tear you up, 'Cause of all the blood you spilled And all the violence you brought to the land, the cities, and the people in 'em.
2.9: Woe to the one who tryna get rich on dirty money, Tryna build a high nest so the drama can't reach him.
2.10: You played yourself—put your fam in shame, Wiped out whole communities, sinned against your own soul.
2.11: Even the bricks in your wall gon' cry out, And the wooden beams gon' testify against you.
2.12: Woe to the one who builds whole cities on bloodshed, Who lay foundations with injustice.
2.13: Don't you know the Lord of Heaven's Armies ain't in that? You workin' yourself to the bone to build bonfires for nothin'.
2.14: But the earth? It's gon' be full of the knowledge of God's glory— Just like the oceans full of water.
2.15: Woe to the one who gets folks drunk, Just so he can peep their shame— Tryna catch folks slippin'.
2.16: You full of shame, not glory. You drinkin'? Go 'head and drink up that same cup— The one God gon' hand you. That shame comin' right back at you, heavy.
2.17: You wrecked Lebanon, now it's gon' come back on you. You scared animals and slaughtered people, Tore up cities and brought violence on everything.
2.18: What's the point of your little idol statue? You made it, now you trust it? That thing can't teach you nothin'—it's a lie. Just wood and metal with no breath in it.
2.19: Woe to you who talkin' to wood like it's alive— Tellin' stone to "wake up." It might be dressed in gold and silver, But it's dead. It ain't got no life in it.
2.20: But the Lord? He sittin' in His holy temple. So the whole earth? Y'all better hush and be still before Him.

3.1: A prayer from the prophet Habakkuk, written with passion and rhythm.
3.2: Lord, I heard what You said—had me shook. Do what You do again in our time, Lord—bring it back! Show Yourself in these years we livin' in. Even when You bring that heat… don't forget to show mercy.
3.3: God showed up from Teman, The Holy One came from Mount Paran. Selah His glory lit up the sky, And the whole earth was filled with His praise.
3.4: His brightness hit like lightning. Power beaming from His hands— That's where His strength was sittin', low-key but ready.
3.5: Disease ran out in front of Him, Plagues followed behind like they knew who was boss.
3.6: He stopped and sized up the whole earth. Just one look had the nations shook. Ancient mountains scattered like dust, Old hills dropped low— His ways been solid from way back.
3.7: I saw Cushan's tents trembling, The people of Midian's curtains shakin' like they caught a chill.
3.8: Lord, was You mad at the rivers? Was the sea gettin' on Your nerves? You rode in on Your horses, Pulled up in Your chariots ready to save.
3.9: Your bow was locked and loaded, You made Your arrows speak with power. Selah You split the land wide open with rivers.
3.10: The mountains saw You and started trembling. Waters overflowed, waves raged. The deep sea hollered out, Lifted up its hands like it knew who was in charge.
3.11: The sun and moon stood still, froze in place, While Your arrows flashed and Your spear blazed through.
3.12: You marched across the land with anger in Your step, Crushed whole nations in Your fury.
3.13: You came to save Your people—yes, Your chosen ones. You struck down the leader of the wicked, Exposed him from top to bottom. Selah
3.14: You used their own weapons on 'em, Took out their village leaders. They came in like a storm tryna wipe me out, Laughin' like it was sweet, feastin' on the helpless.
3.15: You walked right through the sea with Your horses, Stirred up the waters like it was nothin'.
3.16: When I heard all this, my whole body shook. My lips trembled, my bones felt like they was meltin'. I was weak—but I waited in faith, Waitin' for the day of trouble to hit the enemy camp.
3.17: Even if the fig trees don't bloom, No grapes on the vine, Even if the olive harvest fails, And the fields don't produce no food, Even if the sheep vanish from the pen, And the cattle stalls stay empty—
3.18: I'ma still rejoice in the Lord. I'ma turn up in the God who saves me.
3.19: The Lord God is my strength. He gives me feet like a deer, So I can walk high, steady, and strong.
